33.0.0.en: 1- Rejoice in the LORD, O ye righteous: for praise is comely for the upright.

33.0.2.en: 1- Shouting for joy is the highest expression of rejoicing. It is not an inward rejoicing in the heart, but it expresses itself with a loud voice. Those who rejoice are the righteous, whose lives are marked by constant joy in God.

33.0.3.en: 2- The shouting, the rejoicing and the joy are in the Lord, whereas the wicked rejoice in sin, and the carnal rejoice in passing material things. But the righteous rejoice in God; and even if they rejoice in some material thing, they regard it as a gift from God for which they thank Him, and their joy is not in material things in themselves.

33.0.4.en: 3- The upright in heart is the one who keeps God's commandments and rejects evil, so his heart is enlightened and he sees God, and consequently he is drawn to praise Him, and even delights in this praise, for it is the most fitting thing for his life. Indeed, his works and his words in every aspect of life are a testimony to God and praise to His holy name, and not only the words of praise.

33.1.0.en: 2- Praise the LORD with harp: sing unto him with the psaltery and an instrument of ten strings.

33.1.1.en: The harp (oud): one of the oldest stringed instruments. It is a large wooden box with holes in its face, over which the strings are stretched, five pairs of strings.

33.1.2.en: The psaltery: a stringed instrument consisting of a small wooden box over which ten to twelve strings are stretched. In ancient times the strings were played with the fingers or with a bird's quill.

33.1.3.en: 1- David calls us to thank God for His gifts and kindnesses, and to accompany this thanksgiving with melodies played on the harp. Jewish worship was accompanied by musical instruments, because the spiritual level of the Jews needed musical instruments; but in the Church of the New Testament praise became free of musical instruments, as the saints such as St. John Chrysostom and Didymus declared. Musical instruments did not enter Christian worship until the thirteenth century, when the Catholic Church accepted them, and then the Protestant Church. The Orthodox Church, however, still relies on the human throat, and there are only percussion instruments to regulate the voices, namely the cymbals and the triangle.

33.1.4.en: 2- The musical instruments signify man's use of his body and soul, or his tongue and mind, in praising God. As for the ten strings of the psaltery, they signify the name of Jesus, which begins with the letter iota "I", which is the number 10 in Coptic and Greek.

33.1.5.en: 3- The ten strings signify the body and the soul, because the body has five senses and the soul has the inward senses, so the sum of the two is ten; that is, man praises God with his whole being.

33.2.0.en: 3- Sing unto him a new song; play skilfully with a loud noise.

33.2.1.en: 1- The new song presents God, because God's mercies are new every day; therefore we offer Him a song and praise that is renewed every day.

33.2.2.en: 2- The new song is a symbol of the praises of the Church in the New Testament, and also a symbol of the praise of the heavenly ones, as the Book of Revelation tells us (Rev 5:9; 14:3).

33.2.3.en: 3- We hear in the Book of Psalms that all creatures praise God: the mountains, the rivers and all created things. This is a new praise, that is, the submission of all creation to God its Creator, and thanking Him for His kindnesses and His care for it, and man leads this praise.

33.2.4.en: 4- David also calls for the skilful playing to be accompanied by a shout, which is the highest expression of joy and rejoicing, that is, praise with a loud voice. This signifies the praises of the New Testament and their loud cry from the heart, for with spiritual growth man exchanges loud voices for lofty feelings. In the Old Testament we find pictures of this powerful speech of the heart, as when the Lord said to Moses at the Red Sea, when he saw Pharaoh and his army following him and Moses was silent, praying deeply within himself: "Wherefore criest thou unto me?", though he had not opened his mouth (Ex 14:15).

33.3.0.en: 4- For the word of the LORD is right; and all his works are done in truth.

33.3.1.en: 1- The word of the Lord is the Second Hypostasis, Christ our God, and He is right, that is, there is no crookedness in Him, but He is true and perfect.

33.3.2.en: 2- The word of the Lord is right because it teaches us uprightness by means of His commandments, so that we walk uprightly in all our works, in addition to our thoughts and intentions.

33.3.3.en: 3- The word of God draws us and leads us to God, who is uprightness, so that we believe in Him and live with Him in uprightness.

33.3.4.en: 4- The upright word of God makes our inside like our outside, so that we are faithful like God and have no hypocrisy or pretense.

33.3.5.en: 5- All the works of God, that is, His creatures, He made with precision and faithfulness, and all of them testify to Him that He is their Creator, so they call man to believe in God. Whenever he looks at them, he glorifies God.

33.4.0.en: 5- He loveth righteousness and judgment: the earth is full of the goodness of the LORD.

33.4.1.en: 1- God is the Righteous and Holy One, so by nature He loves righteousness, that is, purity and goodness, and consequently He loves all His children who walk in righteousness, and if they sin, they return by repentance to purity.

33.4.2.en: 2- God is perfect in His righteousness and perfect in His justice, so He rejects sin and is repelled by it.

33.4.3.en: 3- Although He is kind to the weak and has mercy on them if they repent, and even calls them to repentance by His mercy, yet He cannot bear the rebellious, the licentious and the sinners who justify their faults and so persist in them. And although He is long-suffering toward them, in the end they must face His justice on the Day of Judgment, to be punished for their sins.

33.4.4.en: 4- God is also perfect in His mercy, and His mercy is unlimited; it is wider than all the sins of mankind and able to forgive all who repent. God comes forward with His mercy toward all the righteous and the wicked, to call them to Himself, but those who enjoy the overflow of His mercies are the righteous.

33.4.5.en: 5- Mercy results from God's love for mankind, so it reaches out toward all; but people, because of their sins, move God's justice to punish them. God is perfect in His mercy and His justice.

33.5.0.en: 6- By the word of the LORD were the heavens made; and all the host of them by the breath of his mouth.

33.5.1.en: The breath of his mouth: the air that comes out of His mouth, that is, the mouth of God.

33.5.2.en: 1- God made the heavens by His command, that is, by His word. With all ease and with His perfect power He made the heavens, and He did not need anyone to help Him in that.

33.5.3.en: 2- By the breath of the mouth of God, that is, by His Holy Spirit, He made the host of the heavens. What is meant by their host is:

33.5.4.en: A - The stars and suns that move with precise order in perfect obedience to God, like the soldier who is bound by the orders of his commander.

33.5.5.en: B - The angels, who obey God's orders and do everything He asks of them.

33.5.6.en: 3- The Holy Trinity, who created the heavens and what is in them, appears in this verse. It mentions the Lord, that is, the Father, His word, that is, the Son, and the breath of His mouth, that is, the Holy Spirit.

33.5.7.en: 4- The Holy God created the heavens holy, so that man might dwell in them after he completes his striving on earth and becomes pure and holy, fit to dwell in heaven. The righteous are heavenly people who live with the mind of heaven while they are on earth, so in the end they deserve that God glorify them in His heavenly Kingdom.

33.6.0.en: 7- He gathereth the waters of the sea together as an heap: he layeth up the depth in storehouses.

33.6.1.en: As an heap: a heap is a mound, or a hill.

33.6.6.en: 1- This verse shows the power of God, who controls the earth and the seas, just as heaven is under His authority. He is able to gather the waters in heaps. This is contrary to the nature of water, as happened when the Red Sea was divided by the hand of Moses, and a road was made between two walls of water, and His people crossed on dry land.

33.6.7.en: 2- The deep seas are very frightening, so that some in ancient times thought them to be the dwelling of Satan; but these depths, that is, the deep waters, God gathers in His storehouses, and He controls them, and even fills them with good things that benefit man, such as fish.

33.6.8.en: 3- The sea signifies the world, which is under God's authority, and He controls it for man's good, so the children of God do not fear the troubles of the world, because God protects them, for He is the Ruler of all.

33.7.0.en: 8- Let all the earth fear the LORD: let all the inhabitants of the world stand in awe of him.

33.7.1.en: 9- For he spake, and it was done; he commanded, and it stood fast.

33.7.2.en: 1- David calls all people to the fear of God, because He is the Creator of all, the life of all is in His hand, and He is also the Ruler of all; therefore the beginning of wisdom is the fear of God.

33.7.3.en: 2- God's greatness appears in that He created everything by His word, and His word is the Second Hypostasis, Christ our God. As soon as God commands, creation comes to be with all its goodness and beauty; therefore all creation ought to glorify Him and all people to praise Him.

33.8.0.en: 10- The LORD bringeth the counsel of the heathen to nought: he maketh the devices of the people of none effect.

33.8.1.en: 11- The counsel of the LORD standeth for ever, the thoughts of his heart to all generations.

33.8.2.en: 1- God created all His creation good and excellent, but after man's fall the wicked thought evil and devised their schemes. God saw how they turned aside and went step by step into evil, but He intervened and brought their plots to nothing when these plots were directed against His godly children, and He rescued them from them, as He brought to nothing the counsel of Ahithophel against David and rescued him from the hand of his son Absalom (2 Sam 17:23), and as He brought to nothing the plot of Haman against the people of God in the days of Esther and Mordecai (Esth 7:10).

33.8.3.en: 2- God's counsel is His thought and His providence. The counsel is that on which people gather in a conference, and here we find God, in His Holy Trinity, having a thought, and this thought is fixed and cannot be changed, and no one, however strong, can bring it to nothing, even if people think that God goes back on His word and changes what He declared, as happened with the people of Nineveh (Jon 3:10). But God's thought is fixed, for He planned to threaten the people of Nineveh and then to return and forgive them when they repent, since God, by His foreknowledge, knows everything, and consequently His thought is fixed.

33.8.4.en: 3- Since God's thoughts are fixed, and the counsel of the wicked can be brought to nothing, the children of God are not alarmed, but pray in every affliction, and God rescues them and brings to nothing the counsel of their enemies, as happened in the days of Hezekiah when Sennacherib attacked him and his army perished.

33.8.5.en: 4- When God created mankind and the whole world, He did not neglect them and leave them afterward, but He placed in His plan the providence and care of His children, so He does not leave the wicked to rule over them; that is, He is able to keep His children in the midst of afflictions and to destroy the wicked. And if His children endure sufferings, or die for His name, He rewards them with eternal life and punishes the wicked.

33.8.6.en: If God is the Ruler of all and orders everything for your good, why do you worry? ..! Rely on Him, ask for your needs and be persistent with Him, for He will order everything for your good.

33.9.s.en: (2) Blessings for those who fear Him

33.9.0.en: 12- Blessed is the nation whose God is the LORD; and the people whom he hath chosen for his own inheritance.

33.9.1.en: 1- God greatly values man's freedom, so the nation that of its own will seeks God as its God receives a great blessing, because God will lead it in the way of salvation, protect it, and let it enjoy His blessings.

33.9.2.en: 2- God also pronounces blessed the one whom He has chosen to be His people, and this choice is based on the people's response to God and their faith in Him. For God knows the hearts, and everything is naked and open before Him.

33.9.3.en: 3- God's choice of His believing children is a choice to give them glories on earth and in heaven. They are His inheritance; He blesses them and establishes them with Him forever.

33.9.4.en: 4- The people of God are His inheritance, for they are the people who loved God out of the whole world. God rejoices in them, because they responded to His love. They alone live for Him, so they are His inheritance.

33.9.5.en: 5- Perhaps in his speaking of the nation there is an allusion to the entry of the Gentiles into the faith, when they choose God as their God, and this is what happened in the New Testament when they believed in Christ our God.

33.9.6.en: 6- We notice that the blessing is due to faith in God, and to the people of God who chose Him as their God, and not to self-righteousness or to personal works apart from faith, that is, the works of the Law.

33.9.7.en: 7- God's choosing of some people means that many were not chosen. This calls us to hold fast to God and to stand firm in the faith, that we may be among the chosen. For if our worship is superficial, or we are lax with sin, we lose our place as children of God.

33.10.0.en: 13- The LORD looketh from heaven; he beholdeth all the sons of men.

33.10.1.en: 14- From the place of his habitation he looketh upon all the inhabitants of the earth.

33.10.2.en: 1- God looks from heaven, for He is higher than all creatures, but His love calls Him to care for His creatures; by His nature He seeks us and condescends to draw near to us, to shepherd us and to care for us. The greatness of His love appeared in His Incarnation, when He united with us and lived among us, to be an example for us of how to live before Him.

33.10.3.en: 2- God sees all people, and nothing is hidden from Him, and He pours out His good things on all; and at the same time, since everything is open before Him, we must fear Him, and if we sin we must hasten to repent to Him, to regain our sonship and enjoy His blessings.

33.10.4.en: 3- God looks into the depths of man, and not only his outward appearance, for He knows the inward intentions of everyone, so He rewards the righteous and also repays the wicked, the pretenders and the hypocrites.

33.10.5.en: 4- The place of God's habitation is not only in heaven, as a declaration of His loftiness, but in His humility He dwells also in the hearts of His children, and He looks upon people who do not believe in Him in order to reveal His light through His children, so that when people see the good works of His children they glorify Him.

33.10.6.en: 5- God's looking at us is a looking of care and love, to look after us by means of His angels, whom He sends to us to declare His love for us and His concern for our salvation.

33.10.7.en: 6- God's looking at us is not mere looking for the sake of knowledge, that is, a passive, useless look, but a positive looking, to care for us and encourage us. When He sees His believing children in His Church, He rejoices in them and leads them in the way of salvation, that they may attain His Kingdom.

33.11.0.en: 15- He fashioneth their hearts alike; he considereth all their works.

33.11.1.en: 1- God is the Fashioner, that is, the Creator of the heart, and He knows man's feelings and inward intentions that move his whole being, and consequently nothing is hidden from Him, so no one can be a hypocrite before Him.

33.11.2.en: 2- God observes all man's works; He sees the upright among them and the crooked. He will surely bless and reward with good the one who walks uprightly. This calls us to carefulness and spiritual striving, however much the wicked surround us.

33.11.3.en: 3- Because God is the Creator of the heart, He is able to create in it the conscience, that is, His voice, to call people to live with Him. He is also able to put His Holy Spirit in them, so that He draws them to faith and works in them with all His power.

33.12.0.en: 16- There is no king saved by the multitude of an host: a mighty man is not delivered by much strength.

33.12.1.en: 17- An horse is a vain thing for safety: neither shall he deliver any by his great strength.

33.12.2.en: 1- David shows that military power is not in the multitude of soldiers, nor in the courage of the commander and his soldiers. Nor is it in the war equipment, the most important part of which is the horses, but in the power of God alone. Sennacherib had many soldiers, and Goliath was very courageous, and Pharaoh in the days of Moses had chariots and many horses, and God destroyed all of these by the hand of His children.

33.12.3.en: 2- Satan comforts the wicked with reliance on the multitude of soldiers, or their courage, or the horses they own, or any material power on which they rely. All these signify Satan, who is nothing if the believers rely on the power of God. Therefore the law of Moses commands not to multiply horses (Deut 17:16), and one of the sins of Solomon was his multiplying of horses, which distanced him from relying on God (1 Kgs 4:26).

33.13.0.en: 18- Behold, the eye of the LORD is upon them that fear him, upon them that hope in his mercy;

33.13.1.en: 19- To deliver their soul from death, and to keep them alive in famine.

33.13.2.en: 1- David concludes his words in this part about God's blessings to His children by speaking of His care for them. He shepherds them and supplies all their bodily and spiritual needs; therefore they live in tranquility, satisfaction and joy, and praise Him continually.

33.13.3.en: 2- Whoever enjoys God's care must have two conditions:

33.13.6.en: For whoever fears God keeps away from every evil, and whoever relies on Him declares his faith in Him.

33.13.7.en: 3- The children of God do not fear death or any affliction, because God is able to deliver them from it; He repels the enemies from them, satisfies them in famine, and solves all their problems; therefore they live in constant security.

33.13.8.en: 4- The satisfaction that God gives them is first of all spiritual satisfaction, before bodily satisfaction. This is by the word of God and His commandments, which rescue His children from spiritual death. And in the Church of the New Testament He satisfies them, above all this, with His most holy Body and Blood.

33.13.9.en: God's blessings are very abundant, and they await you if you rely on Him with true faith. If the fear of God is before your eyes, it will protect you from evil and lead you to repentance if you fall, so that you do not lose your sonship to God, and so enjoy fellowship with Him and your eternal life.

33.14.0.en: 20- Our soul waiteth for the LORD: he is our help and our shield.

33.14.1.en: Our shield: the shield is a defensive instrument that the soldier uses to ward off arrows from himself. It is a piece of wood with a loop at the back, in which the soldier puts his hand and moves it in front of his head and body to protect himself with it.

33.14.2.en: 1- David declares the importance of spiritual striving by saying "we waited for the Lord." He strives relying on the help of the Lord, which must support him and give him victory in the end.

33.14.3.en: 2- In our spiritual warfare God gives us a positive power, which is His help, and a defensive power, which is the shield, so He protects us from the wars of Satan by humility and fasting, and gives us power to overcome him by prayer and all works of goodness.

33.15.0.en: 21- For our heart shall rejoice in him, because we have trusted in his holy name.

33.15.1.en: 1- Reliance on the name of God is reliance on God Himself, for He is a power above every power, and is able to overcome all the powers of the enemies.

33.15.2.en: 2- Repeating the name of God fills the heart with power, and even steadfastness, so that it is not alarmed before the wars of the demons, but conquers them, as we say in the Midnight Praise: "Everyone who says, O my Lord Jesus, is like one who has a sword in his hand and strikes down the enemy" (Monday Psali).

33.15.3.en: 3- Confidence in the power of God during our spiritual wars, and victory over the enemy Satan, gladden the hearts of the children of God, so they hold fast to their striving and experience the renewed work of God in them, and so taste the Kingdom while they are on earth.

33.15.4.en: 4- Reliance on passing material things produces turmoil in the soul, but reliance on God gives steadfastness and inward peace, and consequently enjoyment of fellowship with God, and no alarm at the many wars of the demons.

33.16.0.en: 22- Let thy mercy, O LORD, be upon us, according as we hope in thee.

33.16.1.en: 1- God's mercies have no end; they are very abundant, and God grants them to everyone who strives and relies on Him in proportion to his labor and his holding fast to God, so he enjoys fellowship with God, thanks God in constant praise, and rejoices with inexpressible joy.

33.16.2.en: Do not fear the wars of the devil, for he is very weak before the power of God. Rely on God and ask for His help, for it is very near you and seeks to help you in all the details of your life; indeed, through it you taste a new sweetness in fellowship with God, and so advance with great strides toward the Kingdom.

33.16.3.en: Thanksgiving to God who cares for His godly ones. By David, when he changed his behavior before Abimelech, who drove him away, and he departed. "I will bless the LORD at all times" ... (v. 1) Introduction:

33.16.5.en: 2- When he wrote it: when he was fleeing from the face of Saul and went to the king of the Philistine city of Gath, who was "Achish", or Abimelech (a title of the kings of the Philistines, like the king of Gerar (Gen 20:2)). His servants advised him to seize David, because he was their enemy, so David feigned madness, and Achish disregarded him, and David afterward went to the cave of Adullam (1 Sam 21:10-14) and thanked God for his deliverance.

33.16.6.en: 3- This psalm was written according to the letters of the Hebrew alphabet, so each verse begins with one of these letters.

33.16.7.en: 4- This psalm is considered the last of the five psalms of thanksgiving that began from Psalm 30.

33.16.8.en: 5- The Apostle Peter quoted from it in his first epistle (1 Pet 3:10, 11).

33.16.9.en: 6- The psalm tells us of God's help to those who seek Him and fear Him. Perhaps David prayed when he went to Gath, and when he felt the danger of falling into the hand of Achish, and God guided him to feign madness and made Achish despise him and leave him, because in ancient times they feared madmen, believing that a strange spirit was in them. So he escaped from the hand of the Philistines, and wrote this psalm in thanks to God who rescued him; therefore this psalm suits everyone who meets an affliction or a problem with no solution, and seeks God, who is able to deliver him, and then thanks Him for his deliverance.

33.16.10.en: 7- This psalm is found in the prayer of the Third Hour in the Agpeya, where we remember the descent of the Holy Spirit at this hour, and we thank God who pours out His Holy Spirit on those who seek Him and fear Him, and on everyone who is godly toward Him.
